world.bio: Postdoc in marine biology at a coastal research institute in Lisbon. I extract alginate and carrageenan from locally farmed and beach-cast seaweed and turn them into a cross-linked resin we call SWR-3. Originally from Setúbal, did my PhD in Aveiro, spent a year in Bergen as a visiting student. Outside the lab I run a small Thursday bouldering group and foster a very anxious rescue dog.
skills_assets: Seaweed resin formulation (SWR-3, three batches made so far, lab notebook fully documented)
Access to the institute's UV weathering chamber, a universal testing machine (shared) and a small vacuum oven
Contacts at two seaweed farms near Peniche who sell off-spec biomass cheaply
Small silicone moulds and a 3D-printed mould set for casting discs, bars and tiles
Climbing gym membership and a van-less but bike-friendly life

projects.name: SWR-3 seaweed resin
projects.text: Cross-linked alginate/carrageenan resin with a bio-based plasticiser. Batch 3 cured clearer than batch 1 and 2, with less bubbling after I switched to degassing at 40 C. Tested as cast discs (3 cm) and dog-bone bars only. Next: a 20x20 cm panel, which I have not managed because the mould leaks and the resin shrinks at the edges. The grant reviewers will want a proper object, not discs.

projects.name: Beach-cast biomass survey
projects.text: Counting how much Rugulopteryx and Sargassum washes up on the Cascais coast per month. Paused since July because the field assistant left. Data in a shared spreadsheet, half unlabelled.

notes.text: Lab meeting. Supervisor asked again about the milestone in the grant: 'real-world consumer product prototype' by July. I keep saying we are a materials lab, we characterise things. He said the funders do not read the word 'characterise'. Right now all I have are small cast discs and bars. I could do packaging or cutlery because those are what everyone asks about, but I have no idea who to build with.

Dog woke me at 5 because of the fireworks from the festa. Bolo (the dog) now sleeps on my feet. Fostering is supposed to be temporary, I keep telling myself that. Sofia says I am lying to myself and she is right.

UV chamber results back. 500 h of UV-A/B cycling. Our batch 3 sample yellowed a delta-b of about 3, the commercial bio-epoxy I bought as control went past 9. I stared at the numbers for a while, checked the control twice, same. This might actually be the one property that is better than the incumbent. Not sure it is enough to carry a whole product though.

Bergen call. Tormod has the autumn rain and I have 27 degrees in September. Still 4 more months before I can fly up. He said 'just move here' and I said 'with what job'. We both went quiet. Talked about his sister's wedding instead.

Bouldering Thursday: nine people showed up, two new. Someone fell off the slab and landed badly, nothing broken. I should have a first aid person. Also my left forearm is wrecked. Need to rest, will not.

Grocery list: lentils, tahini, dog food (the grain free one he refuses), AA batteries for the pH meter, pasteis de nata for the lab because Friday. Also email the farm in Peniche about the next biomass shipment, they said October.

Rewrote the grant progress report three times. The honest sentence is 'we have a promising material and no product'. The version I submitted says 'we are validating application pathways across packaging, coatings and structural applications'. I hate it a little.
Tormod's mum sent me a photo of a cinnamon bun and a message in Norwegian. I understood 80%. Counted that as a win. Going to try cooking bacalhau for him in January.

messages.text: Duarte: Inês, the programme officer called. The July milestone is not negotiable, they want to see an actual thing in a hand. Me: I know, I am working on it. Duarte: Work on it faster, please. Me: Cast discs are things. Duarte: Discs are not a product.
Sofia: did you take Bolo out. Me: yes at 7. Sofia: he looked at me like he'd never been out. Me: he does that. Sofia: I love him but he ate my sock. Me: I'll buy you socks.
Tormod: Rain here again. Miss you. Me: Sunny here. Sorry. Tormod: Not funny. Send me a picture of the sea. Me: [photo]. Tormod: ok that is funny.
Marta: the vacuum oven is free tomorrow from 2. Me: I need it for degassing the 20 cm batch. Marta: the mould will leak again. Me: I know. Marta: buy silicone sealant. Me: I did. It is still leaking.

relations.about: Partner in Bergen, works at a fish-feed company. We have been long-distance for 14 months.
Flatmate, nurse at Santa Maria hospital, shift work, loves the dog more than she admits
Supervisor; supportive but under pressure from the funder

constraints: Funding runs out after July of next year, so everything must fit that timeline
Cannot travel mid-week; shared UV chamber is booked in 2-week slots
Will not use anything that needs petroleum-based hardener in the final product
No weekends in the lab if I can avoid it
sensitive: Postdoc salary is below what Tormod thinks it is; I am quietly worried the contract will not be renewed
I get anxious about being the one who 'has a promising material and no product'
